key_insight: UniD shows that a single video model can learn to predict many dense scene properties at once, even when the training data is split across different datasets with incompatible labels. This reduces the need for fully annotated datasets or expensive pseudo-label generation.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the fragmentation of dense video annotations across domain-specific datasets, which makes unified scene understanding difficult. Existing approaches either require fully co-annotated data or rely on costly pseudo-labeling to combine tasks.
method: Introduces UniD, a unified video model for joint prediction of eight dense scene properties from disjoint data.
Trains across heterogeneous datasets without requiring every sample to have all annotations.
Uses a unified formulation to learn geometry, appearance, and semantics together from video.
impact: This matters because it makes multi-task dense prediction more practical and scalable for real-world applications where labels are incomplete and scattered. For practitioners, it can lower annotation costs and simplify building strong unified perception systems.
visual_elements: A pipeline diagram showing multiple disjoint datasets feeding into one unified video model

paper_title: Unified Video Dense Prediction from Disjoint Data
paper_authors: Yihong Sun, Seoung Wug Oh, Jiahui Huang, Bharath Hariharan, Joon-Young Lee
